messages:
sara: Heads-up — we have an alert: multiple admin-role accesses to the key vault in eu-west-1 from a CI runner (ci-runner-42). Triage starting now.
kevin-sre: Link to alert: https://alerts.internal/r/AE12345 — looks like 6 decrypt calls in 3m from same IP.
jon-ops: Containment done: revoked runner tokens, removed runner from pool, disabled the job.
aliyah: Can someone pull KMS audit/decrypt logs for that principal? sharing a quick sample from the logs we grabbed:
```
2026-03-20T10:12:34Z keyvault.decrypt principal=service-account:ci-runner-42 action=Decrypt result=OK region=eu-west-1 request_id=abc123
2026-03-20T10:13:01Z keyvault.decrypt principal=service-account:ci-runner-42 action=Decrypt result=OK region=eu-west-1 request_id=abc124
2026-03-20T10:14:12Z keyvault.decrypt principal=service-account:ci-runner-42 action=Decrypt result=OK region=eu-west-1 request_id=abc125
```
mike: IAM audit shows infra-bot granted ci-runner-42 membership in group `admin-rbac` on 2026-03-14 02:03 UTC. attaching commit id: infra-config#482.
security-bot: Automated alert: IAM change detected — group=admin-rbac actor=infra-bot time=2026-03-14T02:03:12Z.
sara: We need an exec one-pager: what happened, scope, customer impact, and next steps. Quick answers: did any decrypts target customer keys?
aliyah: Preliminary: decrypts appear to be service keys used by infra tests, not customer data keys. Still validating cross-project usage.
kevin-sre: Quick containment steps done. Next: rotate the affected KMS keys for infra project, rotate service-account creds, and harden RBAC so infra-bot cannot auto-add to admin-rbac without human approval.
mike: Draft exec blurb below — feel free to trim: "We detected automated addition of a CI runner to an admin group which led to unauthorized decrypt calls against internal infra keys. Immediate containment: tokens revoked, runner removed, keys rotated for infra project. No evidence of customer data access at this time. Investigation ongoing; mitigations include RBAC approval gates and audit alert tuning."
sara: +1. Also need customer comm decision: only notify if customer-facing keys were touched or if SLA/data access impacted. 
jon-ops: Proposal: notify customers on Dedicated/Private only if evidence of cross-tenant key access. Otherwise send internal advisory and optional partner note.
aliyah: Customer advisory draft (short): "We are investigating an internal key access event that affected infra service keys. We have contained the activity and rotated the affected keys. There is currently no evidence of customer key access or data exposure. We will update by EOD with investigation status and any action items."
kevin-sre: Agreed. Ops: please run a full audit query for any decrypts where key.owner != infra-project in the window 2026-03-14..2026-03-20. Use this query: `SELECT * FROM kms_audit WHERE action='Decrypt' AND timestamp >= '2026-03-14' AND principal='service-account:ci-runner-42'`
mike: Assigning postmortem owner to @sara, timeline doc in docs/incidents/infra-key-admin-2026-03-20.md, will add runbook items for RBAC approval workflow.
ceo: Thx all for quick action. Keep exec updated if any change.
sara: Scheduling incident call in 15m to align on communications. I opened incident ticket IR-2026-0320 and set severity=high. Postmortem owner=sara.
kevin-sre: I'll follow up with a short timeline and a proposed customer notice for Legal review.
jon-ops: I'll close the runner ticket and push a blocking rule to the CI pool.
sara: Great. After call: create remediation PR to remove auto-add in infra-config and require 2 approvals for admin-rbac changes. :thumbsup:
